input_digest.combining_method: sha256 of each file's bytes, then sha256 over those per-file digests concatenated in sorted-basename order. Stated because a digest without its method is not checkable (BUILD_RULES 11.7).

content_hash_canonicalisations.note: TWO canonicalisations, used on DISJOINT hubs: md5(normalise(...)) on HUB_LOCATION and LNK_PARTY_LOCATION (addresses, internal whitespace collapsed) and md5(upper(trim(...))) on HUB_PARTY, LNK_PARTY_ROLE and HUB_ORG_UNIT (nominee and branch NAMES, ends trimmed only). Zero hubs carry both. Emitted as written; unifying them would re-key a hub.

key_rejection.mechanism: shape: CASE over coalesce(<guarded operands>) is not null, then nullif(trim(key),'')
key_rejection.note: Zero is reported as zero. Every key expression in this map evaluates to NULL on an all-blank row under Snowflake semantics, so the outer nullif has nothing to compare against and a predicate of the form key = 'RISK:' could never fire. The per-hub per-feeder drop counts are in audit_mt_key_rejections; they are measured at run time, not here.

findings.detail: THE BUILD CANNOT CURRENTLY BE REGENERATED AT ALL. Every chain generator imports mt_names, whose load_profile REFUSES TO RUN because build_profile.json rev 6 carries 15 keys stage 1 does not consume or acknowledge: clause_remeasurement, collapse_traps_note, collapse_traps_scope_A_18, collapse_traps_scope_B_9, component_kinds_field_note, conventions_artifact, digest_contract_note, document_diff, longest_source_view_cast_example_note, longest_source_view_cast_name, ordinal_artifact, profile_self_assertion, prose_test_counts, renumbering_ordinals_with_no_child_key_reach, workbook_degenerate_column_still_empty_note. So run_all.sh, selfcheck_mt.py and prove_mt_reproducibility.py all exit at step 1, clause 8 could not be re-proved, and the 9 clause-7 regex-firing proofs could not be re-run. THE GUARD IS CORRECT (BUILD_RULES 2.2) and it correctly fires BEFORE the wipe, so nothing was destroyed. WHAT MUST BE DONE: stage 1 reads each of the 15 keys or declares it acknowledged in mt_names.py, then re-runs the deletion proof. Until then the shipped tree is built against profile rev 5 while the profile on disk is rev 6.

ONE modeller question, not eleven blockers, and the de-escalation is measured not argued. Exactly 1 emitted child-key leg over 71 is backed by a renumbering ordinal: SAT_AUG_POLICY_DOCUMENT_DISPATCH src_cdk DISPATCH_SERIAL_NUMBER from SERIAL_NO, and it is the SOLE leg. All four de-escalating facts confirmed independently: 11 map rows on one satellite and one view; the satellite is absent from data_7.js; the map already declares a routed source gap with candidate_stable_key POD_NUMBER and a question_for_source on all 11 rows; and the emitted SQL already carries the UNSTABLE CHILD KEY BUILD_RULES 5.2 marker in both the satellite and its staging model. WHAT MUST BE DONE: answer one question about a proposed satellite grain, namely whether POD_NUMBER is populated and unique per dispatch line. If yes the child key moves to it in one pass. Do not promote or load this satellite until it is answered: an ordinal child key re-attaches history on every insert.

THE src_cdk FIX WAS APPLIED TO CHECK 1 AND NOT TO CHECK 6, so the same defect survives in the coverage number. check 6 still tests only col in src_payload. Measured on this LOB: 12 of the 17 pairs it counts as missed ARE in the vault, as child-key legs, so coverage reads 425 of 442 when the true reach is 437 of 442. The consequence is worse than a wrong percentage: 12 exemption lines now exist to suppress a gap that is not a gap, and each of those lines says so in its own comment. WHAT MUST BE DONE: apply the same src_payload UNION src_cdk comparison in check 6, then delete the 12 carried_as_cdk exemption lines, which will no longer be needed.

WHAT THE GREEN COVERS, stated because it is smaller than it looks. check 1 examines 103 of the 234 built satellites; the 131 augmented satellites are outside its population entirely, because want is built only from map rows whose satellite and attribute are canonical in data_7.js. Proved by injection: renaming a payload column on an AUGMENTED satellite leaves check 1 at exit 0, while the same rename on a canonical satellite yields exit 1 on checks 1 and 6. This is not a defect in the gate, since augmented satellites are proposals rather than canonical structures, but it bounds the claim and should be printed alongside the satellite counts.

THE PUBLISHED 52 OF 91 DOES NOT REPRODUCE, and I am reporting what I measured rather than the number I was asked to carry forward. Population stated: 51 LNK call sites in target and augmentation resolved_key.expression, 91 legs recovered by balanced-paren splitting, which agrees with the published leg total exactly. Of those 91, exactly 34 carry a name token and every one is of the form HUB_X equals; 57 carry none; and ZERO legs contain an equals sign anywhere other than those 34. So not-named-for-a-hub is 57 of 91, not 52 of 91, and the missing 5 cannot be recovered by widening the name search. Under a different and defensible scope, hub-BOUND by explicit name OR by matching a harvested hub key expression per BUILD_RULES 4, the figure is 19 of 91 unbound. Note also that this build states 39 and 40 for the same quantity in one file: link_leg_census.named_for_a_hub is 39 while reconciliation.build_parser_lnk_named_legs is 40. WHAT MUST BE DONE: stage 1 states the slot set and the binding rule its 39 comes from, or adopts one of the two scopes measured here.

NARROWED, NOT RETIRED, and re-derived from the SIBLING BUILD rather than the profile. 234 satellites here, 45 on travel_dv_dbt, 35 written by BOTH. Retired on the column NAME: bare HASHDIFF on 234 of 234 here and 45 of 45 there, 0 name disagreements, and 0 disagreements on src_pk, grain or src_cdk across all 35. NOT retired on the CONTENT: the hashdiff input list differs on 34 of the 35; only SAT_POLICY_CLASSIFICATION agrees. WHAT MUST BE DONE: one modeller decision per shared satellite on whose payload set the shared hashdiff is computed over, before any shared load. Same name with different contents is the dangerous half, because every check that compares names reports clean.

VERIFIED LIVE and independently of the blocked chain, so the detector zero is a JUDGED zero. The control file 04_column_map.pre_docfix.json digests to 81cd1f46a6fb6248dc897e602644b56d6f460a109b4ec1c458a2d43da71857f5, exactly the recorded BD13_CONTROL_DIGEST, and it is not byte-identical to the live map at 6350105 versus 6378022 bytes. An independent reimplementation of the prefix-split probe returns 1 finding on the control, HUB_DOCUMENT DOCUMENT_ID appearing both bare and under the DOC namespace, which is precisely the expected finding, and 0 on the live map. Nothing needs doing; this is the carried item confirmed.

THE SCOPE IS RESOLVED, so this is no longer undetermined. The profile figure of 20 reproduces exactly under one explicitly stated scope: a satellite-leg pair whose rendered discriminator is ONE distinct string across ALL rows carrying the leg, with no minimum row count, over a denominator of 57 pairs carrying a child-key leg at all. My list matches the profile list on 19 of 20 elements. WHAT MUST BE DONE: record that scope beside the 20 and retire the competing 18 and 9, which come from adding a more-than-one-row and a more-than-one-view restriction. AND SPLIT THE CLASS: 11 of the 20 are column-bearing expressions that are textually identical across rows but vary per row at load, so they are not collapse traps at all. Only 9 are literal-backed, corroborated independently by the map own leg_backing field. Reporting 20 overstates the hazard by more than double.

PROMOTION CANDIDATE, raised from the verifier own defect. My first notation pattern file, authored through a shell heredoc, silently acquired three 0x08 BACKSPACE bytes where word boundaries were meant, so two of ten patterns could not match and their zeros were meaningless. That is the maximus_property PLACEHOLDER_CK defect in BUILD_RULES 12, committed live by the step enforcing it, and it was caught only by a byte-level check of my own probe file. check_patterns already detects exactly this, but nothing points it at a verifier scratch probe. WHAT MUST BE DONE: have the verifier run check_patterns over its OWN probe files before trusting any zero, and say so in the stage-2 contract. This is the third estate occurrence of the same byte.

MY OWN DEFECT, found and repaired, and it is a contract issue for this stage rather than a build finding. My check_internal injection wrote a real model file and restored it in TEXT mode, which on Windows rewrote 19 line endings from LF to CRLF. My own assertion that the file was restored byte-identical was ALSO made through a text-mode read, so it normalised the very difference it was meant to detect and reported True. The damage was caught only by recomputing the whole-tree digest, which had moved to 6bbd6ddc. I converted the file back to LF and the tree digest returned to 0c79ac108b4271d488008d1bc4562728e6da8e1c3f509b2a9f537c3cfb323d5d, matching the recorded proof over 1044 files. WHAT MUST BE DONE: any on-disk probe reads and writes bytes, never text, and the whole-tree digest is recomputed after every on-disk probe. Prefer in-memory injection, which is what the other probes used and why they left no trace.

THE FIRST VERSION OF MY OWN SECOND IMPLEMENTATION AGREED WITH THE GATE FOR THE WRONG REASON. It counted a bare pass-through column name in a select list as a DEFINITION and never read the YAML derived-columns form, so an attribute that a wide stage writes as cast-null in YAML still read as live through the satfeed bare mention. Two implementations agreeing means nothing if the second has a blind spot in the same direction. Caught because an injection applied 0 definitions and the number did not move. After repair, both report 0 over 1355 attributes, both fire on both tracks, and both name the injected attribute. RECORD: agreement between implementations is evidence only once each has been shown to fail independently.

A MEASURED SCOPE LIMIT, not a defect, but it changes what a PASS means. The declared flag set by a SOURCED marker stays true until the next line beginning with a hash, so one provenance line discharges every count below it to the end of its section. My first injection, appended at the end of the file, was therefore silent, and I nearly recorded that silence as proof the gate works. Re-injected under a new heading it fires correctly with 2 findings. WHAT MUST BE DONE: consider narrowing the discharge to the adjacent block, or print how many counts were discharged by provenance so a reader can see how much the PASS is actually asserting.

TWO FIGURES IN THE PROFILE FOR ONE QUANTITY. layer_sizing gives total_views_needing_a_cast 115 and walk_only_casts_required 51 alongside views_carrying_map_rows 62, but 62 plus 51 is 113, not 115; the 51 is the rev-3 figure carried beside a rev-6 total, and the method_delta_note explains the 113-to-115 change without updating the sub-count. Stage 1 reports walk_only_casts 53, which does reconcile. Measured independently: 115 cast models over 115 distinct source views, 62 views carrying map rows, 0 mapped views without a cast. WHAT MUST BE DONE: recompute walk_only_casts_required under the rev-6 method or delete it.

NO GAP, and the one apparent gap resolves. All 62 views carrying any map row have a cast, and all 56 carrying a MAPPED row do. 50 resolvers over 50 distinct start views, 0 start views with more than one resolver. 0 name-injectivity failures over 115 casts and 115 source views, proved by injecting a second real source view into one cast model. 25 unpivot models against 593 literal-backed legs over 36 views, so the unpivot layer is not manufactured where no column-as-instance family exists. Of 16 distinct spine destinations over 2390 arrows, 4 have no cast of their own: MEMBER_DETAILS 77 arrows, PROPOSER_DETAILS 67, QUOTE_PARAM_DETAILS 2, POLICY_DETAILS 1. All four are the UNQUALIFIED SEGMENT form stage 0 recorded, every one is a segment of its own origin view name, and every origin HAS a cast, so the walk is fully covered by the segment fallback and none of the four is a missing layer.

THE WITHDRAWAL WAS CORRECT, and I confirm it by measurement. vault_tools/accepted_uncovered.txt holds 36 non-comment lines in total: maximus_health_v2_dv_dbt 16, maximus_travel_dv_dbt 17, maximus_travel_dv_dbt 3. So the earlier claim that 34 of 35 of health_v2 exemption lines were stale was a file-wide count attributed to one project, and stage 3 was right to withdraw it. Health V2 has 16 lines, not 35. The underlying gap stands: the shared file still has no per-project integrity guard and is merged by hand.
